analysis: This PR changes only documentation (docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md and docs/developer/test.md): date bumps, a clarification of CBv2PagedPrefixRestore reserved-token behavior, mention of Gemma TP scopes, and a new 'Gemma TP prompt prefixes' section (lines 1268-1320) plus a test-checks section in test.md. I found no code, config or permission changes, so no direct security regression. Security-relevant claims in the new docs were checked against the threat model, mainly T-041 (cross-tenant prefix cache, at-rest SSD tier, SEC-035) and TB-007. The Gemma TP section says prefix scopes include the request's tenant partition via Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes (line 1281). It says a request with the cache off votes on neither rank (1282) and that a failed request keeps nothing (1280). It says records use the shared encrypted SSD tier with owner-only directories, TTL and write cap (1308-1310), and that restores need a second sealed bilateral confirmation (1283). These claims match the existing cluster tenant-partition design (lines 1019-1068) and do not weaken the T-041 posture as documented. The SSD records are described as native (exact) for Gemma. I could not verify that the underlying Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix implementation, which is outside the supplied evidence, actually enforces tenant digests on both the resident and SSD tiers, or that the 'on'/'off' load agreement refuses mismatched peers. Integration review should confirm those when the code lands. The new Gemma TP cache is a new persistent at-rest surface (SSD records for Gemma TP ranks) that arguably extends the T-041 scope description; the threat model's T-041 text could mention the cluster tiers, but this is a documentation-only observation and not a finding. test.md unit 67373c0eff1153bd:0 had only metadata and a patch excerpt, with no executable change visible.
